title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter II of the 1986 notes is about topological realizations of 'réseaux' (networks). The basic building block is a 'ficelle' (string) F=(X,{A,B}): a space X with two disjoint closed 'extremities' A and B. A 'ligne' C of F, distinct from the extremities, cuts F into two subdivided ficelles F_{A,C}=(X_{A,C},{A,C}) and F_{B,C}=(X_{B,C},{B,C}). The previous page proves a betweenness lemma: if D is a line of F_{B,C}, then C is a line of F_{A,D}. This gives an order structure A<C<D<B on lines. It then treats model case 2): X homeomorphic to a ball, i.e. I×B^n≃B^{n+1}, with extremities {0}×B^n and {1}×B^n and lines homeomorphic to B^n.

This page treats model case 3), 'Être homéom. à S^n'. Take S^n with two distinct points a,b (antipodal if one wishes; this remark is struck out). Draw a '2-decomposition' by an S^{n-1}, i.e. an embedded (n-1)-sphere C separating a from b. Then S^n = X_{a,C} ∪_C X_{b,C}, two discs glued along C. The figure is the case n=1: a circle with points a and b, and C = S^0 consisting of two cut points, one at the top and one at the bottom.

Refinement: away from the extremities one may require that C be bicollared. That is, C has a neighbourhood homeomorphic to C×]-1,1[ with C = C×{0}. The two 'rives' (banks) C×]-1,0[ and C×]0,1[ must lie respectively in the two component pieces X_{A,C} and X_{B,C}. This tameness condition rules out wild cuts (Alexander horned sphere type) and makes the local two-sidedness of a cut explicit.

The next page formalizes 'rives' for an arbitrary closed subset A⊂X. It defines Rives(A,X) = colim_{V⊃A} Comp(V∖A) = Γ(A, i_*F_2|A). When A has a tubular neighbourhood, this equals Comp of the boundary of the tube. It then introduces the 'découpage' (cutting) of X along A via a relative Spec of i_*F_2. The purpose of the whole development is a tame, axiomatic theory of cutting spaces along hypersurfaces, as the basis for the topological realization of networks/graphs.
errors: Minor: for the circle picture (n=1), the separating set C = S^0 consists of two points; the text's 'un S^{n-1}' is consistent with this, but the dimension indexing (whether the ambient sphere is S^n or S^{n-1}) is ambiguous in the handwriting and transcription.

Without the bicollar condition, an embedded S^{n-1} need not bound discs on both sides (wild spheres, n≥3). Grothendieck adds the collar requirement only as an option ('on peut aussi exiger'), so the plain 2-decomposition case needs that hypothesis for the pieces to be balls (generalized Schoenflies, Brown).

ideas.what: Model of a 'ficelle' on S^n: two marked points separated by an embedded (n-1)-sphere, cutting S^n into two pieces
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition of a sphere along a separating codimension-1 sphere (Jordan–Brouwer / Schoenflies)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jordan, Brouwer, Schoenflies; generalized Schoenflies by M. Brown (1960) and Mazur

ideas.what: Requirement that the cut C be bicollared, C×]-1,1[, with the two banks lying in the two pieces
ideas.modern_name: Bicollared / two-sided locally flat hypersurface; collar neighbourhood
ideas.where_published: Spirit of 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this specific formulation

ideas.what: Notion of 'rives' (banks) of a cut, leading on the next page to the sheaf-theoretic definition Rives(A,X)=Γ(A,i_*F_2) and a cutting construction
ideas.modern_name: Local components of complement / links; cutting a space along a subspace (normalization-like 'découpage')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Freudenthal ends, local homology); cutting along hypersurfaces is standard in 3-manifold topology

missed.claim: Part of an axiomatic, tame-topology theory of 'ficelles' (strings) and their cuttings as topological realizations of networks/graphs, with sphere and ball models. It belongs to the never-written tame topology program of the Esquisse. This page itself contains only the model case and the collar condition.
missed.quote: On peut aussi exiger, dans un lieu distinct des extrémités, que la structure de X au voisinage de C soit celle de C×]-1,1[
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents how Grothendieck intended to axiomatize 'cutting along hypersurfaces' for his topologie modérée. It is mainly of historical interest; the mathematics on the page is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page presents a standard model example (a sphere cut by an equatorial sphere) and the standard bicollar condition. Its interest is only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished tame-topology program on realizations of networks.
transcription_corrections: '3) Ex[?] homogène[?] : S^n' should read '3) Être homéom. : S^n' (parallel to '2) Être homéomorphe à B^n' on the previous page).
'une structure[?] de 2 décomposition[?]' reads 'une structure de 2-décomposition par un S^{n-1}'.
The struck-out parenthesis reads '(par ex. antipodiques, si on veut)'.
Final line 'X_{A,C}, X_{B,C}' is written with capital A and B as subscripts (B overwritten).
